children: Markets opened on a cautious note on Friday, October 30, 2026, weighed down by a sharp sell-off in global technology stocks and surging crude oil prices, even as domestic institutional buying provided a cushion. The Sensex, which had closed at 74,151.04 on Thursday, opened at 74,199.69 and was trading at 74,164.21, up just 13.17 points or 0.02 per cent, while the Nifty 50, which had closed at 22,936.75, opened at 22,964.50 and was quoting at 22,941.70, up a marginal 4.95 points or 0.02 per cent at 9.20 am.

Among the top gainers on the Nifty 50, Trent led the pack, surging 5.48 per cent to ₹3,018.40, after opening at ₹3,018 and touching a high of ₹3,060. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries rose 2.01 per cent to ₹1,796.40, while Infosys gained 1.41 per cent to ₹1,162.65. IndiGo climbed 1.39 per cent to ₹4,739.90, and Tata Consultancy Services added 1.21 per cent to trade at ₹2,508.

On the losing side, defence electronics maker Bharat Electronics Ltd fell 1.62 per cent to ₹364, while Coal India declined 1.50 per cent to ₹387.20 on heavy volumes of over 39.52 lakh shares. Nestlé India slipped 1.09 per cent to ₹1,175.70, Shriram Finance dropped 1.05 per cent to ₹832.30, and Tata Steel shed 1.03 per cent to ₹167.72.

The subdued opening followed a weak overnight session on Wall Street, where technology stocks bore the brunt of selling. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.4 per cent to close at 26,185, the S&P 500 fell 0.3 per cent to 7,720, and the Dow Jones slipped 0.25 per cent to 52,343. Alphabet plunged approximately 12.6 per cent — its worst single-day decline since its IPO — erasing roughly $480 billion in market capitalisation, after disappointing ad and search revenue growth and guiding 2026 capital expenditure at $195–205 billion. Amazon dropped around 7 per cent in extended trading on higher spending and slowing online growth, while Intel plunged approximately 23 per cent on a weak fourth-quarter revenue forecast and soft PC demand.

"The results renewed Wall Street's doubts about near-term returns on AI investment," noted Devarsh Vakil, Head of Prime Research at HDFC Securities, adding that "Nasdaq 100 futures were down roughly 2 per cent overnight."

Adding to the pressure, crude oil prices rose about 1.75 per cent to $103.5 a barrel, driven by Gulf and Hormuz supply risks. Brent crude was hovering near $115–117 a barrel, according to separate market commentary. "The crude oil headwind is getting stronger with Brent rising above $117," said Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. "There are reports of the US likely resuming strikes against Iran after the mid-term elections which is due on November 3rd."

WTI crude's rise into the $102–103 range is a particular concern for India. "For India, persistently elevated crude oil prices remain a key macroeconomic headwind, weighing on investor risk appetite," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. The rupee had already depreciated 4 paise to close at 95.26 on Thursday, though central bank intervention and foreign institutional buying in equities offered partial support.

On the macroeconomic front, the US Federal Reserve held its target rate at 3.75–4.00 per cent on a 10-2 vote at its latest policy meeting, with both dissenters favouring a hike. US third-quarter GDP expanded at an annualised 3.4 per cent, beating expectations, but September PCE inflation climbed to 3.6 per cent year-on-year, keeping rate-cut expectations firmly off the table. Markets are now pricing a 75–80 per cent chance of a December rate hike. The European Central Bank, meanwhile, kept its key rate unchanged at 2.5 per cent.

"The impressive 3.4 per cent US Q3 GDP numbers and high PCE inflation number at 3.6 per cent means that US bond yields will remain elevated and will continue to attract safe haven funds," Vijayakumar said, flagging continued pressure on emerging market flows.

Asian markets were broadly lower, with Japan's Nikkei 225 falling more than 1 per cent and South Korea's KOSPI declining over 3 per cent, pressured by technology and semiconductor stocks. The Bank of Japan was concluding its two-day policy meeting and was widely expected to hold rates at 1.25 per cent.

On the domestic institutional front, DIIs net bought equities worth ₹1,924 crore on Thursday, their second consecutive session of purchases, while FIIs turned net sellers with outflows of ₹943 crore, snapping a two-session buying streak.

Technically, the Nifty faces immediate resistance at 23,100–23,200, with support at 22,800–22,850. "Sustained buying above 23,000 is essential to confirm stronger upward momentum," said Ponmudi R. Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, noted that "the breakout has improved the short-term technical structure, although follow-through buying remains important." For Bank Nifty, which closed at 54,909.65 on Thursday, resistance is placed at 55,300–55,500 and support at 54,500–54,700.

title: Markets open flat amid tech sell-off, crude surge; Trent leads Nifty gainers
